findings.note: Old 2025 page: in 2024-25 Monahan had 38 assists in 54 games, played about 19 minutes a night and led the NHL in 5-on-5 assists per 60. Nothing current was found to show he still has that role, and the +310 price may mean his role is smaller now.

Old January 2025 report: Columbus put Monahan on injured reserve with an upper-body injury. It shows he has been hurt before, but no current injury, practice or lineup news for Oct 18, 2026 turned up in the search.

RotoWire (Oct 9) says all three of Coleman's points have come with the man advantage, where he leads the Wild's second power-play unit. It expects his hot start to fade toward his usual mid-to-high 30s point pace. His power-play role is the main risk to the Under.

ESPN's game log shows 3 points (2 G, 1 A, all on the power play) in 6 October games while averaging about 15:35 of ice time. He was scoreless in 3 of his last 5 listed games, including both games on Oct. 10 and Oct. 12. The Oct. 15 game against St. Louis was not shown.

NHL.com's projected lineup for Oct. 15 had Coleman on Minnesota's second line with Danila Yurov and Maxim Shabanov, a middle-six role. No injury was noted. I found no Oct. 18 lineup, injury report, Columbus matchup info, or published pick on this market.

Rotowire notes say his rookie season ended with 5 assists in 37 games (9 points), mostly on the power play. The risk to the Under is that he moved to the first power-play unit late in the season, scored 7 of his 9 points in the last 14 games, and was expected to play full time in 2026-27.
ESPN's career stats show a low assist rate (4 assists in about 33-34 games in 2025-26, 3 of them on the power play) while he averaged about 16:30 of ice time. No current-season game log was found.

An Oct 11, 2026 Flames video shows Parekh with the team as a Sport Calgary Ambassador. Only one search went through, so no dated injury, lineup, power-play unit or analyst-pick reporting was found for this game.

A Sep 20, 2026 RotoWire/CBS note says Farabee should get a bigger role in 2026-27 after Blake Coleman was traded, and he skated on Mikael Backlund's second-line wing in camp. It also expects Calgary to finish near the bottom of the standings.

Last season Farabee scored 38 points (20 goals) in 82 games while playing in all situations. Late-season notes said he had top-six minutes but recently no power-play time, which limited his scoring, and he went four straight games without a point before his last game.
Farabee had two goals and an assist in a 5-4 win over Carolina on Mar 8, 2026. The same page also shows streaky output, including several six-game point droughts on a low-scoring Flames team.
